\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Cryptography.MPC.BGW.Protocol}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Degree-preserving resharing]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.Resharer}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b005,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b006
}
\statementsource{AL17}{pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b002}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.Resharer}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing, TCSlib.Shamir.Party}
Let $F$ be a field and let $d$ be a natural number. A resharer assigns to each party $i$
and value $x \in F$ a value for each receiving party, such that the resulting assignment
is a degree-$d$ sharing of $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Degree reduction]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.degreeReduce}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b001,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b002,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b003,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b004
}
\statementsource{AL17}{
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b005,
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p023-b001
}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.degreeReduce}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombineCoeff}
Given a resharer $R$ of degree $d$ and a finite set $A$ of parties, the degree-reduction
map sends an assignment $u$ of field elements to parties to the assignment whose value
at party $j$ is $\sum_{i\in A} \lambda_{A,i} R_i(u(i),j)$, where $\lambda_{A,i}$ is the
recombination coefficient for $A$ and $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sharing After Degree Reduction]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.isSharing_degreeReduce}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b001,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b002,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b003,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b004
}
\statementsource{AL17}{
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p023-b001,
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p027-b002
}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.isSharing_degreeReduce}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.degreeReduce, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.recombine_eq, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.smul, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.sum, TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombineCoeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, and let $u$ be a sharing of $z$ given by evaluations of a polynomial
of degree at most $2d$. If the finite party set $A$ has cardinality at least $2d+1$,
then applying the specified degree-reduction procedure to $u$ gives a sharing of $z$ by
evaluations of a polynomial of degree at most $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[BGW circuit evaluation]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b004,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b008,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b001,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b004
}
\statementsource{AL17}{
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p016-b001,
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p018-b003
}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.degreeReduce, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit, TCSlib.Shamir.Party}
Given a degree-$d$ resharer $R$, a finite set $A$ of parties, and party-indexed input
shares for each input label, evaluate a circuit over $F$ as a party-indexed assignment:
inputs use their supplied shares, constants are shared uniformly as the constant,
addition and scalar multiplication act pointwise, and multiplication is followed by the
degree-reduction map defined using $R$ and $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of an input wire]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_input}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_input}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval, TCSlib.Shamir.Party}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field with decidable equality, let $\iota$ be an input-index type, let
$d\in\mathbb N$, let $R$ be a degree-$d$ resharer, and let $A$ be a finite set of
parties. For every party-indexed input assignment $\mathrm{inp}$ and input label $i$,
the BGW evaluation of the circuit consisting of the input wire $i$ is exactly the
supplied assignment $\mathrm{inp}(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a constant circuit]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_const}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b004,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b006
}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_const}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval, TCSlib.Shamir.Party}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field, let $\iota$ be a type, let $R$ be a resharer, and let $A$ be a
finite set of parties. For any input assignment and constant $c\in F$, the evaluation of
the constant circuit is the constant function on parties with value $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation preserves addition]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_add}
\statementsource{BGW88}{pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b008}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_add}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit, TCSlib.Shamir.Party}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field, let $\iota$ be a type, let $R$ be a resharer, and let $A$ be a
finite set of parties. For any input assignment and circuits $a,b$, the partywise
evaluations of the circuit that adds $a$ and $b$ equal the sum of their partywise
evaluations.
\end{theorem}

\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval, TCSlib.MPC.BGW.isSharing_degreeReduce, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit.eval, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.add, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.mul, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.smul, TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_const}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $\iota$ be a type, let $d$ be a natural number, let $R$ be a
resharer, and let $A$ be a finite set of parties with $2d+1\le |A|$. Suppose each input
wire $i$ is assigned a degree-$d$ sharing of its value $v(i)$. Then, for every circuit
$C$, the BGW evaluation of $C$ is a degree-$d$ sharing of the ordinary evaluation of $C$
on the values $v$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval, TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_isSharing, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit.eval, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.recombine_eq, TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombine}
\difficulty{2}
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero field elements with $2d+1\le
|A|$, and suppose each input wire $i$ is supplied with shares that are evaluations of a
polynomial of degree at most $d$ whose value at $0$ is $v(i)$. For every arithmetic
circuit $C$, recombining the shares produced by the BGW evaluation of $C$ on these
inputs yields $C$ evaluated at the secret inputs $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear circuit evaluation is independent of the resharer]
\lean{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_of_isLinear}
\label{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_of_isLinear}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.MPC.BGW.Resharer, TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval, TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_add, TCSlib.MPC.BGW.bgwEval_smul, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit, TCSlib.MPC.Circuit.IsLinear, TCSlib.Shamir.Party}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $\iota$ be a type, let $d$ be a natural number, let $R$ and $R'$
be resharers, and let $A$ be a finite set of parties. For every input assignment and
every linear circuit, its BGW evaluations using $R$ and $R'$ agree as functions on
parties.
\end{theorem}
